name: app.R
content:
# HEE evidence map — interactive app
#
# Thematic gallery of the full figure catalogue (size & growth, topics, methods,
# geography, gaps vs burden, reach & funding, country maps, trends, priority-setting,
# journal figures), a multi-variable Explorer (any combination of income, region,
# disease, evaluation type, design, approach, QALY use, open access, scope),
# per-country profiles, and a methods summary.
#
# Data: app_data.rds, built by R/09-build-shiny-data.R (run from projects/hee/analysis).
# Figures: www/*.webp, copied from figures/ by the same script, which also copies
# R/intensity.R beside this file so filtered ratios use the project-wide formulas.
# Launch: shiny::runApp("shiny") (see DEPLOY.md).
#
# Run locally:  shiny::runApp("shiny", launch.browser = TRUE)

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(shiny); library(bslib); library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2); library(plotly); library(DT); library(scales); library(htmltools)
})

# The bundle and the shared ratio helpers live beside this file under runApp("shiny");
# the fallbacks also allow launching from the analysis root.
D <- readRDS(if (file.exists("app_data.rds")) "app_data.rds" else "shiny/app_data.rds")
source(if (file.exists("intensity.R")) "intensity.R" else "R/intensity.R")

INC_LV  <- rev(D$meta$inc_lv)   # display order: high -> low
PAL_INC <- D$meta$pal_inc       # canonical palette, shipped in the bundle
YEARS <- D$meta$years
REGIONS <- sort(unique(stats::na.omit(D$elig_geo$un_region)))

fmt_n <- function(x) comma(x, big.mark = ",")

# ---- gallery registry ----------------------------------------------------------
# One entry per figure: file (in www/), title, caption. Sections are thematic:
# size & growth, topics & diseases, methods, geography & authorship, gaps vs burden,
# open access & funding, country maps, trends over time, priority-setting for
# funders, and the journal figures.

GALLERY <- list(
  list(
    title = "Size & growth",
    blurb = sprintf("How much research is there, and what kind? %s health economic evaluations were
             extracted (%d–%d); %s are eligible for analysis. These panels carry the headline:
             the growth of the corpus, and how its evaluation-method mix has shifted.",
             fmt_n(D$meta$n_extracted), D$meta$years[1], D$meta$years[2],
             fmt_n(D$meta$n_studies)),
    figs = list(
      list(file = "fig_growth.webp", title = "Cumulative growth",
           caption = "The field keeps doubling: half of everything published since 2010 appeared
                      after 2020 (2026 flagged partial)."),
      list(file = "fig_method_stream.webp", title = "Evaluation-method composition over time",
           caption = "Cost-utility rose from 45% to 54% of annual output while cost-effectiveness
                      fell from 34% to 25%.")
    )),
  list(
    title = "Topics & diseases",
    blurb = "Topic, disease and intervention — the subject of the evidence. OpenAlex topics cover
             88% of the corpus; MeSH disease groups cover 63% (harvested subset, base declared on
             each figure). The emergent-theme maps come from abstract embeddings, not MeSH.",
    figs = list(
      list(file = "fig_topic_landscape.webp", title = "Topic landscape",
           caption = "OpenAlex subfields grouped by field — the research areas of the field in
                      one circular view."),
      list(file = "fig_disease_circular.webp", title = "Disease landscape",
           caption = "MeSH disease groups: share of studies, coloured by LMIC/HIC lean."),
      list(file = "fig_disease_method.webp", title = "Disease × evaluation method",
           caption = "How each disease area is evaluated — cost-utility vs cost-effectiveness
                      heat map."),
      list(file = "fig_transition.webp", title = "Epidemiological transition of research",
           caption = "LMIC research shifted communicable → NCD past the burden shares; injuries
                      stayed at ~1% of research vs 11% of burden."),
      list(file = "fig_topicmap_income.webp", title = "Thematic landscape by income",
           caption = "Embedding topic map (UMAP + HDBSCAN) coloured by each theme's LMIC share:
                      theme space segregates — malaria 91% LMIC vs dementia 6%."),
      list(file = "fig_topicmap.webp", title = "Thematic landscape",
           caption = "The plain theme-space map of the corpus, before income colouring."),
      list(file = "fig_theme_rank.webp", title = "Emergent themes ranked by income",
           caption = "The 15 most- and 15 least-LMIC themes: the two ends never overlap
                      (33–91% vs 3–13% LMIC).")
    )),
  list(
    title = "Methods & decision-usefulness",
    blurb = "What gets measured, and how well — the decision-usefulness core. How evidence flows
             from design to method to outcome, which comparable metric is used where, and whether
             abstracts foreground the elements a decision-maker needs.",
    figs = list(
      list(file = "fig_alluvial.webp", title = "Source → analysis → outcome",
           caption = "Alluvial of design basis → evaluation type → outcome family: how evidence
                      flows through the field."),
      list(file = "fig_metric.webp", title = "The comparable-metric currency",
           caption = "QALYs for rich settings, DALYs for poor: cross-income comparability is
                      broken at the metric level."),
      list(file = "fig_model_time.webp", title = "Model vs measurement over 17 years",
           caption = "The drift toward model-based (vs directly measured) evaluations, by income
                      group."),
      list(file = "fig_decision.webp", title = "Decision-framing in abstracts",
           caption = "ICER 39%, threshold 22%: few abstracts foreground decision elements — and
                      LMIC studies report them slightly more than HIC, not less."),
      list(file = "fig_forest.webp", title = "What predicts decision-usefulness",
           caption = "Adjusted odds ratios: income, design basis, disease and year predict
                      generic-metric use. Observational, never causal.")
    )),
  list(
    title = "Geography & authorship",
    blurb = "Where the research is about, and who leads it. Income-comparative figures use
             extracted geography only (the affiliation proxy is income-biased in availability).",
    figs = list(
      list(file = "fig_dotmap.webp", title = "Global proportional-symbol map",
           caption = "Where the evidence sits: bubbles by country study count, coloured by income
                      group (Berrang-Ford style, Robinson)."),
      list(file = "fig_worldmap.webp", title = "World map of output",
           caption = "The global distribution of eligible evaluations by country."),
      list(file = "fig_top_producers.webp", title = "Top producers: volume vs per-capita",
           caption = "Two-rank slope — who leads by count vs by output per person."),
      list(file = "fig_authorship_pattern.webp", title = "Who leads research about each setting",
           caption = "Local / mixed / foreign authorship stacked by income: research about poor
                      countries is often led from abroad."),
      list(file = "fig_collab_chord.webp", title = "Collaboration structure",
           caption = "Income × income co-authorship chord: how the collaboration network runs
                      between groups.")
    )),
  list(
    title = "Gaps vs disease burden",
    blurb = "The map's whole point: research vs the burden of disease (GBD 2023 DALYs, country
             totals and 22 Level-2 causes) and vs health spending (IHME, PPP 2022).",
    figs = list(
      list(file = "fig_burden.webp", title = "Evidence per unit of burden",
           caption = "Studies per 100k DALYs vs total burden: an 18× gap between the best- and
                      worst-served countries."),
      list(file = "fig_spending.webp", title = "Evidence per dollar of spending",
           caption = "Studies per US$1bn of health spending (PPP 2022 × latest World Bank
                      population, mostly 2025)."),
      list(file = "fig_burden_disease_companion.webp", title = "Research share vs burden share, by disease",
           caption = "Maternal-neonatal research runs at 3.6× its burden share in HIC vs 0.37× in
                      LMIC; injuries 0.21× in LMIC."),
      list(file = "fig_burden_disease.webp", title = "Burden-weighted disease mismatch (journal finish)",
           caption = "The same mismatch in Lancet register: study share vs DALY share by income."),
      list(file = "fig_deficit.webp", title = "Largest absolute evidence deficits",
           caption = "Studies vs burden-expected: India +4,847 short, Nigeria +1,205,
                      Indonesia +920 …"),
      list(file = "fig_injustice.webp", title = "High burden, low research",
           caption = "The burden × evidence plane with a burden-proportional diagonal; size =
                      population. The editorial closer."),
      list(file = "fig_inequality.webp", title = "Within-LMIC inequality",
           caption = "Lorenz curve: the least-served half of LMIC burden holds 16% of the
                      evidence; top 5 countries hold 55%; Gini 0.50.")
    )),
  list(
    title = "Open access & funding",
    blurb = "How the evidence is packaged and reached. Open-access status covers 93% of the
             eligible corpus (post DOI-supplement harvest); the funder field covers ~28% and is a
             floor, not a census.",
    figs = list(
      list(file = "fig_openaccess.webp", title = "Open access over time",
           caption = "46% → 80% (2010–24); LMIC research is more open than HIC research."),
      list(file = "fig_funder_funders.webp", title = "Who funds it",
           caption = "Top funders by studies, split by income focus: most big funders are
                      HIC-focused; Gates dominates LMIC; Wellcome has a real LMIC share.")
    )),
  list(
    title = "Country maps",
    blurb = "The cartographic collection: eligible-only counts, World Bank population, GBD 2023
             burden, extracted geography, Robinson projection. Share maps show only countries
             with ≥5 studies (grey below).",
    figs = list(
      list(file = "fig_map_burden.webp", title = "Research intensity vs burden",
           caption = "Studies per 100k DALYs, diverging scale — the map form of the burden
                      mismatch figure."),
      list(file = "fig_map_bivariate.webp", title = "Burden × evidence bivariate",
           caption = "The high-burden/low-evidence corner lights up; dark purple is high on both
                      (big countries), not missing data."),
      list(file = "fig_map_deserts.webp", title = "Evidence deserts",
           caption = "0 / 1–5 / 6–20 / 21+ studies: 20 countries carry a burden but have no
                      evaluation at all."),
      list(file = "fig_map_authorship.webp", title = "Who studies whom",
           caption = "Share of studies with a local author — parachute research, mapped."),
      list(file = "fig_map_model.webp", title = "Model-based vs measured",
           caption = "The LMIC lean on modelled evidence, by country."),
      list(file = "fig_map_openaccess.webp", title = "Open access by country",
           caption = "Share of output that is open access (93% base)."),
      list(file = "fig_map_growth.webp", title = "Where the evidence is youngest",
           caption = "Share of studies published since 2018."),
      list(file = "fig_map_method.webp", title = "Dominant evaluation method",
           caption = "Cost-utility North / cost-effectiveness South."),
      list(file = "fig_map_disease.webp", title = "Disease atlas",
           caption = "Eleven small-multiple maps, one per GBD disease group; log counts, so the
                      disease contrast is the point.")
    )),
  list(
    title = "Trends over time",
    blurb = "Comparative time-series on the year dimension (2010–2025; 2026 partial, dropped).
             Income-comparative panels use single-country extracted geography with a known
             income group.",
    figs = list(
      list(file = "fig_equity_time.webp", title = "Equity over time",
           caption = "LMIC share of annual output rose 16% → 36% — still far below their 83%
                      burden share."),
      list(file = "fig_qaly_time.webp", title = "QALY-metric convergence",
           caption = "LMIC QALY use 15% → 49% vs HIC 51% → 59%: the gap narrowed, ~10pp
                      remains."),
      list(file = "fig_reach_time.webp", title = "Reach over time",
           caption = "Cumulative share of each income group's countries with ≥1 evaluation:
                      high-income covered early, low-income reached last (28% → 96%)."),
      list(file = "fig_method_stream.webp", title = "Method streamgraph",
           caption = "Evaluation-type composition: cost-utility 45% → 54%, cost-effectiveness
                      34% → 25%."),
      list(file = "fig_decision_time.webp", title = "Decision-usefulness over time",
           caption = "All four abstract signals rose; threshold most (12% → 29%) — still a
                      minority.")
    )),
  list(
    title = "Priority-setting for funders",
    blurb = "Built for a funder asking where the next pound buys the most missing evidence.
             Ranked by gap, never by cost-to-close: there is no cost or research-funding-amount
             data. Proportionality to burden is a reference point, not a target.",
    figs = list(
      list(file = "fig_funder_opportunity.webp", title = "Opportunity matrix",
           caption = "Disease × income research-to-burden ratio: injuries, maternal,
                      cardiovascular and neurological in lower-income settings are the reddest."),
      list(file = "fig_funder_scorecard.webp", title = "Priority scorecard",
           caption = "Burden × intensity scatter plus the ranked deficit bar — the shortlist."),
      list(file = "fig_funder_capacity.webp", title = "Capacity-building quadrant",
           caption = "Burden × local-authorship share: the high-burden, <75%-local set — fund
                      people, not just studies."),
      list(file = "fig_funder_trajectory.webp", title = "Self-correcting vs stuck",
           caption = "LMIC research-to-burden ratio, era-1 → era-2 arrows: injuries and maternal
                      are stuck below burden and worsening."),
      list(file = "fig_funder_funders.webp", title = "Funder landscape",
           caption = "Top funders by studies, split by income (~28% coverage — a floor, not a
                      census).")
    )),
  list(
    title = "Journal figures",
    blurb = "The tight journal set: each figure carries one finding, greyscale-safe, legends
             present, uncertainty shown.",
    figs = list(
      list(file = "paper01.webp", title = "PRISMA flow",
           caption = "Study selection: 44,941 extracted → 38,199 eligible evaluations."),
      list(file = "paper02.webp", title = "Decision-relevance cascade",
           caption = "Studies meeting each successive criterion for decision-relevance."),
      list(file = "paper03.webp", title = "Density within & between income groups",
           caption = "Studies per 10 million people by country, faceted by income; area =
                      population."),
      list(file = "paper04.webp", title = "Disease composition by era and income",
           caption = "The epidemiological transition of the research, journal finish."),
      list(file = "paper05.webp", title = "Disease × income heat map",
           caption = "Which diseases dominate the evidence in each income group."),
      list(file = "paper06.webp", title = "In-country authorship",
           caption = "Is the evidence produced in the countries it is about? Point + CI by
                      income."),
      list(file = "paper07.webp", title = "Evidence vs disease burden",
           caption = "Studies per 100k DALYs vs burden, by income — the 18× gap."),
      list(file = "paper08.webp", title = "Research attention vs burden, by disease",
           caption = "Study share vs DALY share across the 11 disease groups.")
    ))
)

FIG_INDEX <- list()
for (sec in GALLERY) for (f in sec$figs) FIG_INDEX[[f$file]] <- f

fig_card <- function(f) {
  div(class = "fig-card",
      tags$img(src = f$file, alt = f$title, loading = "lazy",
               onclick = sprintf("Shiny.setInputValue('fig_open', '%s', {priority: 'event'})",
                                 f$file)),
      div(class = "fig-body",
          div(class = "fig-title", f$title),
          div(class = "fig-caption", f$caption)))
}

gallery_panel <- function(sec) {
  nav_panel(sec$title,
            div(class = "theme-wrap",
                p(class = "theme-blurb", HTML(sec$blurb)),
                div(class = "fig-grid", lapply(sec$figs, fig_card))))
}

# ---- explorer variable registries ----------------------------------------------
TREND_VARS <- c("Income group" = "income", "UN region" = "un_region",
                "Evaluation type" = "econ_eval_type", "Design basis" = "design_basis",
                "Model vs measured" = "model_label", "Uses QALY" = "qaly_label",
                "Open access" = "oa_label", "Geographic scope" = "geo_scope",
                "Nothing (total)" = "none")
GEO_VARS <- c("income", "un_region")          # live on study x country rows
COMP_VARS <- c("Evaluation type" = "econ_eval_type", "Design basis" = "design_basis",
               "Model vs measured" = "model_label", "Uses QALY" = "qaly_label",
               "Open access" = "oa_label", "Geographic scope" = "geo_scope",
               "Era" = "era", "Topic domain" = "topic_domain",
               "Disease group" = "grp", "Reports an ICER" = "icer_label",
               "Reports a threshold" = "thresh_label")
STACK_VARS <- c("None" = "", "Era" = "era", "Model vs measured" = "model_label",
                "Uses QALY" = "qaly_label", "Geographic scope" = "geo_scope")
MAP_METRICS <- c("Studies" = "studies", "Studies per 100k DALYs" = "per100k",
                 "Studies per US$1bn spending" = "per_bn",
                 "Studies per million people" = "per_million")
SCAT_X <- c("Total DALYs (GBD 2023)" = "dalys", "Population" = "pop",
            "Health spending, PPP US$bn (2022)" = "total_spend_bn")
SCAT_Y <- c("Studies" = "studies", "Studies per 100k DALYs" = "per100k",
            "Studies per US$1bn spending" = "per_bn",
            "Studies per million people" = "per_million")

# ---- UI --------------------------------------------------------------------------
ui <- tagList(
  tags$head(tags$link(rel = "stylesheet", href = "styles.css")),
  page_navbar(
  title = "HEE evidence map",
  theme = bs_theme(
    version = 5,
    primary = "#1f5fa8", secondary = "#6b7280",
    bg = "#faf9f6", fg = "#1c2733"
  ),
  fillable = FALSE,

  # ---- OVERVIEW ----
  nav_panel(
    "Overview",
    layout_column_wrap(
      width = 1, heights_equal = "row",
      card(
        card_body(
          h2(class = "hero-title", "Where health-economic evidence exists — and where it is missing"),
          p(class = "hero-text",
            "This app maps the global evidence base of health economic evaluations — studies that
             compare two or more ways of delivering care on both costs and consequences. ",
            strong(fmt_n(D$meta$n_extracted)), " evaluations published ",
            D$meta$years[1], "–", D$meta$years[2], " were extracted; ",
            strong(fmt_n(D$meta$n_studies)),
            " full economic evaluations are eligible for analysis. The ",
            em("Gallery"), " presents the full figure catalogue by theme, the ",
            em("Explorer"), " crosses any variables in the corpus, the ",
            em("Country profile"), " opens a single setting, and ",
            em("Methods"), " explains how the map is built."),
          h2(class = "glance-title", "The evidence base at a glance"),
          layout_column_wrap(
            width = 1/4,
            value_box("Eligible full evaluations", fmt_n(D$meta$n_studies), theme = "primary"),
            value_box("Years covered",
                      paste0(D$meta$years[1], "–", D$meta$years[2]), theme = "secondary"),
            value_box("Countries studied", fmt_n(D$meta$n_countries_named),
                      "named in extracted geography", theme = "info"),
            value_box("Journals", fmt_n(D$meta$n_journals),
                      "of the harvested set", theme = "secondary"),
            value_box("Use QALYs", paste0(round(D$meta$pct_qaly), "%"), theme = "success"),
            value_box("Model-based", paste0(round(D$meta$pct_model), "%"), theme = "info"),
            value_box("Single-country studies", paste0(round(D$meta$pct_single), "%"),
                      theme = "secondary")
          )
        )
      ),
      layout_column_wrap(
        width = 1/3,
        card(card_body(class = "p-0",
          tags$img(src = "fig_dotmap.webp", class = "hero-img", alt = "Global dot map",
                   onclick = "Shiny.setInputValue('fig_open', 'fig_dotmap.webp', {priority: 'event'})"))),
        card(card_body(class = "p-0",
          tags$img(src = "fig_burden.webp", class = "hero-img", alt = "Evidence vs burden",
                   onclick = "Shiny.setInputValue('fig_open', 'fig_burden.webp', {priority: 'event'})"))),
        card(card_body(class = "p-0",
          tags$img(src = "fig_transition.webp", class = "hero-img", alt = "Epidemiological transition",
                   onclick = "Shiny.setInputValue('fig_open', 'fig_transition.webp', {priority: 'event'})")))
      )
    )
  ),

  # ---- GALLERY ----
  do.call(nav_menu, c(list("Gallery"), lapply(GALLERY, gallery_panel))),

  # ---- EXPLORER ----
  nav_panel(
    "Explorer",
    layout_sidebar(
      sidebar = sidebar(
        width = 300,
        title = "Filter the corpus",
        sliderInput("x_years", "Publication years", min = YEARS[1], max = YEARS[2],
                    value = YEARS, sep = "", step = 1),
        selectizeInput("x_income", "Income group", choices = INC_LV, multiple = TRUE,
                       options = list(placeholder = "All groups", plugins = list("remove_button"))),
        selectizeInput("x_region", "UN region", choices = REGIONS, multiple = TRUE,
                       options = list(placeholder = "All regions", plugins = list("remove_button"))),
        selectizeInput("x_disease", "Disease area", choices = D$disease_grps, multiple = TRUE,
                       options = list(placeholder = "All areas", plugins = list("remove_button"))),
        selectizeInput("x_evaltype", "Evaluation type",
                       choices = sort(unique(D$studies$econ_eval_type)), multiple = TRUE,
                       options = list(placeholder = "All types", plugins = list("remove_button"))),
        selectizeInput("x_design", "Design basis",
                       choices = sort(unique(D$studies$design_basis)), multiple = TRUE,
                       options = list(placeholder = "All designs", plugins = list("remove_button"))),
        radioButtons("x_model", "Approach", inline = TRUE, selected = "All",
                     choices = c("All", "Model-based", "Measured")),
        radioButtons("x_qaly", "QALY use", inline = TRUE, selected = "All",
                     choices = c("All", "Uses QALY", "No QALY")),
        radioButtons("x_oa", "Open access", inline = TRUE, selected = "All",
                     choices = c("All", "Open access", "Not open")),
        selectInput("x_scope", "Geographic scope",
                    choices = c("All", sort(unique(D$studies$geo_scope))), selected = "All"),
        actionButton("x_reset", "Reset filters", class = "btn-outline-secondary btn-sm mt-2"),
        hr(),
        p(class = "text-muted small",
          "Every filter combines. Open-access status is known for 93% of the corpus; “Unknown”
           records are excluded when a side is chosen. Country panels count a multi-country
           study once per country it is about.")
      ),
      layout_column_wrap(
        width = 1/4,
        value_box("Studies in view", textOutput("v_studies"), theme = "primary"),
        value_box("Countries in view", textOutput("v_countries"), theme = "info"),
        value_box("Model-based", textOutput("v_model"), theme = "secondary"),
        value_box("Uses a QALY", textOutput("v_qaly"), theme = "success")
      ),
      layout_column_wrap(
        width = 1/2, heights_equal = "row",
        card(card_header("Studies over time"),
             card_body(
               selectInput("x_trend_by", "Colour by", choices = names(TREND_VARS),
                           selected = "Income group", width = "220px"),
               plotlyOutput("x_trend", height = 320))),
        card(card_header("Map — intensity by country"),
             card_body(
               selectInput("x_map_metric", "Metric", choices = names(MAP_METRICS),
                           selected = "Studies", width = "220px"),
               plotlyOutput("x_map", height = 320))),
        card(card_header("Composition of the filtered corpus"),
             card_body(
               layout_columns(col_widths = c(5, 4, 3),
                 selectInput("x_comp_var", "Variable", choices = names(COMP_VARS),
                             selected = "Evaluation type"),
                 selectInput("x_comp_stack", "Group by", choices = names(STACK_VARS),
                             selected = "None"),
                 selectInput("x_comp_mode", "Measure", choices = c("Count" = "n", "Share (%)" = "pct"),
                             selected = "n")),
               plotlyOutput("x_comp", height = 340))),
        card(card_header("Countries — any two variables"),
             card_body(
               layout_columns(col_widths = c(6, 6),
                 selectInput("x_scatter_x", "X axis", choices = names(SCAT_X),
                             selected = "Total DALYs (GBD 2023)"),
                 selectInput("x_scatter_y", "Y axis", choices = names(SCAT_Y),
                             selected = "Studies per 100k DALYs")),
               plotlyOutput("x_scatter", height = 340)))
      ),
      card(card_header("Top countries in this view"),
           card_body(DTOutput("x_table", height = 320)))
    )
  ),

  # ---- COUNTRY PROFILE ----
  nav_panel(
    "Country profile",
    layout_sidebar(
      sidebar = sidebar(
        width = 300,
        title = "Country",
        selectizeInput("c_iso3", NULL,
                       choices = setNames(D$countries$iso3, D$countries$country),
                       selected = "IND",
                       options = list(placeholder = "Pick a country…")),
        uiOutput("c_facts_ui")
      ),
      layout_column_wrap(
        width = 1/4,
        value_box("Eligible studies", textOutput("c_n"), theme = "primary"),
        value_box("Per 100k DALYs", textOutput("c_daly"), theme = "info"),
        value_box("Per US$1bn spending", textOutput("c_spend"), theme = "secondary"),
        value_box("Per million people", textOutput("c_percap"), theme = "success")
      ),
      layout_column_wrap(
        width = 1/2,
        card(card_header("Output over time — country vs income-group mean"),
             card_body(plotlyOutput("c_trend", height = 320))),
        card(card_header("Disease mix — country vs income group"),
             card_body(plotlyOutput("c_mix", height = 320)))
      )
    )
  ),

  # ---- METHODS ----
  nav_panel(
    "Methods",
    div(class = "methods-wrap",
      card(card_header("What counts as an eligible study"),
           card_body(
             p("The map covers ", strong("full economic evaluations"), " of health-care delivery
               published from 1 January 2010 onward: studies that compare two or more ways of
               delivering care on ", strong("both costs and consequences"), ". The unit of
               analysis is the study; the analysis is descriptive and, where it compares research
               against disease burden, ecological."),
             p("Title/abstract screening was machine-learning based, with a measured sensitivity
               of 0.962 against a human reference set. Partial evaluations (cost-minimisation,
               budget-impact, cost-of-illness) and records unclear at extraction are excluded, so
               the analysis population is full evaluations by construction. Studies whose
               consequence is a non-clinical metric (e.g. diagnostic accuracy, utilisation) are
               kept and flagged."),
             tags$table(class = "methods-table",
               tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th("Selection funnel"), tags$th("Records"))),
               tags$tbody(
                 tags$tr(tags$td("Identified"), tags$td("1,154,050")),
                 tags$tr(tags$td("Screened at title/abstract"), tags$td("1,119,811")),
                 tags$tr(tags$td("Confident includes"), tags$td("45,588")),
                 tags$tr(tags$td("Extracted"), tags$td("44,941")),
                 tags$tr(tags$td("Excluded — partial evaluations"), tags$td("−3,388")),
                 tags$tr(tags$td("Excluded — unclear at extraction"), tags$td("−2,819")),
                 tags$tr(tags$td("Excluded — duplicate DOIs"), tags$td("−535")),
                 tags$tr(tags$td(strong("Analysis population")), tags$td(strong("38,199")))
               ))
           )),
      card(card_header("Data sources"),
           card_body(
             tags$table(class = "methods-table",
               tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th("Input"), tags$th("Source"))),
               tags$tbody(
                 tags$tr(tags$td("Study metadata & bibliometrics"),
                         tags$td("CrossRef + OpenAlex + PubMed + NLM MeSH harvest (~93% coverage
                                  of the eligible population)")),
                 tags$tr(tags$td("Income groups"), tags$td("World Bank API classification")),
                 tags$tr(tags$td("Population"),
                         tags$td("World Bank SP.POP.TOTL (latest observation, mostly 2025)")),
                 tags$tr(tags$td("Disease burden"),
                         tags$td("IHME GBD 2023 DALYs (country totals + 22 Level-2 causes)")),
                 tags$tr(tags$td("Health spending"),
                         tags$td("IHME Health Spending 1995–2022 (total health expenditure per
                                  capita, PPP 2022; national total = per-capita × latest
                                  population)")),
                 tags$tr(tags$td("Disease coding"),
                         tags$td("MeSH C-tree any-topic headings mapped to 11 groups, crosswalked
                                  to GBD Level-2 causes")),
                 tags$tr(tags$td("Research topics"),
                         tags$td("OpenAlex topic taxonomy plus an emergent theme model (abstract
                                  embeddings → UMAP → HDBSCAN)"))
               )),
             p(class = "methods-note", "Reference data are fetched from dated sources, never
               bundled snapshots.")
           )),
      card(card_header("Rules that keep the numbers honest"),
           card_body(
             p(strong("Extracted geography only."), " The author-affiliation proxy is accurate
               where it applies, but its availability is income-biased — merging it would inflate
               the headline burden gap from 17.8× to 25.8×, so it is excluded from every income
               figure."),
             p(strong("Multi-country studies count once per country"), " in the country panels,
               and every figure declares whether its denominator is studies or study–country
               pairs."),
             p(strong("Countries without a World Bank income group are visibly absent,"),
               " never zero-filled as “0 studies”."),
             p(strong("Burden proportionality is a reference point, not a normative target:"),
               " research allocation also reflects tractability, intervention cost and the stock
               of existing evidence."),
             p(strong("Abstract decision-signals measure what abstracts report, not what studies
               did"), " — “not reported” is not “not done”."),
             p(strong("MeSH uses any-topic headings:"), " major-topic marking jumps at the 2020
               harvest boundary and would manufacture a trend.")
           )),
      card(card_header("Limitations"),
           card_body(
             p("The corpus is effectively English-only (99.8%). Geography is missing for ~33% of
               studies; country-level figures cover the placeable subset. Harvest coverage is
               partial (47–93% depending on field) and declared per figure. Comparisons of
               research to burden are ecological. Extraction fields disagree for 8.3% of studies,
               handled by conservative disqualification. The 50,661 records unsure at
               title/abstract are held out of the population pending a handling policy.")
           ))
    )
  )
))

# ---- SERVER ------------------------------------------------------------------
server <- function(input, output, session) {

  # ---- figure modal ----
  observeEvent(input$fig_open, {
    f <- FIG_INDEX[[input$fig_open]]
    req(f)
    showModal(modalDialog(
      title = f$title,
      tags$img(src = f$file, class = "modal-fig", alt = f$title),
      p(class = "fig-caption mt-2", f$caption),
      footer = modalButton("Close"),
      size = "xl", easyClose = TRUE
    ))
  })

  # ---- Explorer reactives ----
  # The year slider fires on every drag tick; debounce so the heavy chain
  # (38k-row filter -> geo join -> five rendered outputs) runs once on release.
  years_d <- shiny::debounce(reactive(input$x_years), 400)

  # study-level filters (everything except the country attributes)
  flt_studies_base <- reactive({
    s <- D$studies |>
      filter(year >= years_d()[1], year <= years_d()[2]) |>
      mutate(icer_label   = if_else(has_icer == 1, "ICER reported", "Not reported"),
             thresh_label = if_else(has_threshold == 1, "Threshold reported", "Not reported"))
    if (length(input$x_evaltype)) s <- s |> filter(econ_eval_type %in% input$x_evaltype)
    if (length(input$x_design))   s <- s |> filter(design_basis %in% input$x_design)
    if (input$x_model != "All")   s <- s |> filter(model_label == input$x_model)
    if (input$x_qaly != "All")    s <- s |> filter(qaly_label == input$x_qaly)
    if (input$x_oa != "All")      s <- s |> filter(oa_label == input$x_oa)
    if (input$x_scope != "All")   s <- s |> filter(geo_scope == input$x_scope)
    if (length(input$x_disease)) {
      ids <- D$elig_disease |> filter(grp %in% input$x_disease) |>
        pull(record_id) |> unique()
      s <- s |> filter(record_id %in% ids)
    }
    s
  })

  # study x country rows (country panels; a multi-country study appears once per country)
  flt_geo <- reactive({
    g <- D$elig_geo |> filter(record_id %in% flt_studies_base()$record_id)
    if (length(input$x_income)) g <- g |> filter(income %in% input$x_income)
    if (length(input$x_region)) g <- g |> filter(un_region %in% input$x_region)
    g
  })

  # study-level panels: when income/region filters are active, restrict to studies
  # about the selected countries, so every filter truly combines across all panels
  flt_studies <- reactive({
    s <- flt_studies_base()
    if (length(input$x_income) || length(input$x_region)) {
      s <- s |> filter(record_id %in% flt_geo()$record_id)
    }
    s
  })

  flt_by_country <- reactive({
    flt_geo() |> distinct(record_id, iso3) |> count(iso3, name = "studies") |>
      right_join(D$countries |>
                   select(iso3, country, income, un_region, pop, dalys, total_spend_bn),
                 by = "iso3") |>
      mutate(studies = coalesce(studies, 0L),
             per100k = per_100k_dalys(studies, dalys),
             per_bn  = per_bn_usd(studies, total_spend_bn),
             per_million = per_million_pop(studies, pop))
  })

  observeEvent(input$x_reset, {
    updateSliderInput(session, "x_years", value = YEARS)
    updateSelectizeInput(session, "x_income", selected = character(0))
    updateSelectizeInput(session, "x_region", selected = character(0))
    updateSelectizeInput(session, "x_disease", selected = character(0))
    updateSelectizeInput(session, "x_evaltype", selected = character(0))
    updateSelectizeInput(session, "x_design", selected = character(0))
    updateRadioButtons(session, "x_model", selected = "All")
    updateRadioButtons(session, "x_qaly", selected = "All")
    updateRadioButtons(session, "x_oa", selected = "All")
    updateSelectInput(session, "x_scope", selected = "All")
  })

  # ---- value boxes ----
  output$v_studies   <- renderText(fmt_n(nrow(flt_studies())))
  output$v_countries <- renderText(fmt_n(n_distinct(flt_geo()$iso3)))
  output$v_model <- renderText({
    s <- flt_studies()
    paste0(round(100 * mean(s$model_label == "Model-based", na.rm = TRUE)), "%")
  })
  output$v_qaly <- renderText({
    s <- flt_studies()
    paste0(round(100 * mean(s$qaly_label == "Uses QALY", na.rm = TRUE)), "%")
  })

  # ---- trend ----
  output$x_trend <- renderPlotly({
    cb <- TREND_VARS[[input$x_trend_by]]
    if (cb == "none") {
      s <- flt_studies() |> count(year)
      p <- ggplot(s, aes(year, n)) +
        geom_line(linewidth = 0.9, colour = "#1f5fa8") +
        labs(x = NULL, y = "studies")
    } else if (cb %in% GEO_VARS) {
      s <- flt_geo() |> filter(!is.na(.data[[cb]])) |>
        distinct(record_id, year, .data[[cb]]) |>
        count(year, .data[[cb]])
      p <- ggplot(s, aes(year, n, colour = .data[[cb]])) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
        labs(x = NULL, y = "studies", colour = NULL)
      if (cb == "income") p <- p + scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_INC, drop = FALSE)
    } else {
      s <- flt_studies() |> count(year, .data[[cb]])
      p <- ggplot(s, aes(year, n, colour = .data[[cb]])) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
        labs(x = NULL, y = "studies", colour = NULL)
      if (cb == "oa_label") {
        p <- p + scale_colour_manual(values = c("Open access" = "#1baf7a",
                                                "Not open" = "#eb6834",
                                                "Unknown" = "#adb5bd"), drop = FALSE)
      }
    }
    ggplotly(p + theme_minimal(base_size = 12), tooltip = c("x", "y", "colour")) |>
      layout(legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.18), margin = list(t = 20, b = 60))
  })

  # ---- map ----
  output$x_map <- renderPlotly({
    d <- flt_by_country()
    m <- MAP_METRICS[[input$x_map_metric]]
    if (m == "studies") {
      z <- log10(d$studies + 1)
      cs <- list(c(0, "#f1f3f5"), c(0.0001, "#c6dbef"), c(0.5, "#2a78d6"), c(1, "#08306b"))
      cb <- list(title = "studies<br>(log)",
                 tickvals = log10(c(0, 1, 10, 100, 1000) + 1),
                 ticktext = c("0", "1", "10", "100", "1000"))
      txt <- paste0(d$country, "<br>", fmt_n(d$studies), " studies")
    } else {
      z <- d[[m]]
      cs <- list(c(0, "#f7fbff"), c(0.5, "#6baed6"), c(1, "#08306b"))
      cb <- list(title = gsub(" ", "<br>", input$x_map_metric))
      txt <- paste0(d$country, "<br>", fmt_n(d$studies), " studies<br>",
                    round(z, 2), " ", tolower(input$x_map_metric))
    }
    plot_geo() |>
      add_trace(data = d, locations = ~iso3, z = z, text = txt, hoverinfo = "text",
                colorscale = cs, marker = list(line = list(color = "#ffffff", width = 0.3)),
                colorbar = cb) |>
      layout(geo = list(projection = list(type = "robinson"), showframe = FALSE,
                        showcoastlines = FALSE, bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)"),
             margin = list(t = 0, b = 0))
  })

  # ---- composition ----
  output$x_comp <- renderPlotly({
    xv <- COMP_VARS[[input$x_comp_var]]
    sv <- STACK_VARS[[input$x_comp_stack]]
    pct <- input$x_comp_mode == "pct"
    s <- flt_studies()
    base <- if (xv == "grp") {
      D$elig_disease |> filter(record_id %in% s$record_id) |>
        left_join(s |> select(record_id, era, model_label, qaly_label, geo_scope),
                  by = "record_id")
    } else s
    if (nzchar(sv) && sv != xv) {
      d <- base |> count(.data[[xv]], .data[[sv]], name = "n")
      names(d)[names(d) == xv] <- "x"
      names(d)[names(d) == sv] <- "s"
      d <- d |> filter(!is.na(x), !is.na(s))
    } else {
      sv <- NULL
      d <- base |> count(.data[[xv]], name = "n")
      names(d)[names(d) == xv] <- "x"
      d <- d |> filter(!is.na(x))
    }
    if (is.null(sv)) {
      d <- d |> mutate(v = if (pct) 100 * n / sum(n) else n) |>
        arrange(desc(v)) |>
        mutate(x = factor(x, levels = rev(unique(x))))
      p <- ggplot(d, aes(x, v)) +
        geom_col(fill = "#1f5fa8", width = 0.72) +
        labs(x = NULL, y = if (pct) "share of filtered studies (%)" else "studies")
    } else {
      d <- d |> group_by(x) |> mutate(tot = sum(n)) |> ungroup() |>
        mutate(x = factor(x, levels = rev(unique(x[order(tot)]))))
      p <- ggplot(d, aes(x, n, fill = s)) +
        geom_col(position = if (pct) "fill" else "stack", width = 0.72) +
        labs(x = NULL, y = if (pct) "share within category (%)" else "studies", fill = NULL) +
        { if (pct) scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) }
    }
    note <- if (xv == "grp") " · a study can sit in several disease groups" else ""
    ggplotly(p + coord_flip() + theme_minimal(base_size = 12),
             tooltip = c("x", "y", "fill")) |>
      layout(legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.22),
             margin = list(t = 10, b = 70),
             annotations = list(list(
               text = paste0(input$x_comp_var, note), xref = "paper", yref = "paper",
               x = 0, y = 1.06, xanchor = "left", showarrow = FALSE,
               font = list(size = 11, color = "#6b7280"))))
  })

  # ---- scatter ----
  output$x_scatter <- renderPlotly({
    xv <- SCAT_X[[input$x_scatter_x]]
    yv <- SCAT_Y[[input$x_scatter_y]]
    d <- flt_by_country() |>
      filter(studies > 0, !is.na(.data[[xv]]), .data[[xv]] > 0,
             !is.na(.data[[yv]]), .data[[yv]] > 0, !is.na(income))
    p <- ggplot(d, aes(.data[[xv]], .data[[yv]], colour = income,
                       text = paste0(country, "<br>", fmt_n(studies), " studies"))) +
      geom_point(alpha = 0.8, size = 1.9) +
      scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
      scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_INC, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
      labs(x = paste0(input$x_scatter_x, " (log)"),
           y = paste0(input$x_scatter_y, " (log)")) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
    ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text") |>
      layout(legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.2), margin = list(t = 20, b = 60))
  })

  # ---- table ----
  output$x_table <- renderDT({
    flt_by_country() |>
      filter(studies > 0) |>
      arrange(desc(studies)) |>
      transmute(Country = country, Income = income, Region = un_region, Studies = studies,
                `Per 100k DALYs` = round(per100k, 2),
                `Per US$1bn` = round(per_bn, 2),
                `Per million` = round(per_million, 2)) |>
      head(25)
  }, options = list(dom = "t", pageLength = 25, scrollY = TRUE), rownames = FALSE)

  # ---- Country profile ----
  c_row <- reactive({
    req(input$c_iso3)
    D$countries |> filter(iso3 == input$c_iso3)
  })
  c_inc_median <- reactive({
    r <- c_row()
    D$countries |> filter(income == r$income) |>
      summarise(m_daly = median(per100k_dalys, na.rm = TRUE),
                m_bn   = median(per_bn_usd, na.rm = TRUE),
                m_mil  = median(per_million, na.rm = TRUE))
  })

  output$c_facts_ui <- renderUI({
    r <- c_row()
    pairs <- list(list("Income group", r$income),
                  list("UN region", if (!is.na(r$un_region)) r$un_region else "—"))
    if (!is.na(r$pop))
      pairs <- c(pairs, list(list("Population",
                                  paste0(fmt_n(round(r$pop / 1e6)), " M"))))
    if (!is.na(r$dalys))
      pairs <- c(pairs, list(list("Disease burden",
                                  paste0(fmt_n(round(r$dalys / 1e6)), " M DALYs (2023)"))))
    if (!is.na(r$total_spend_bn))
      pairs <- c(pairs, list(list("Health spending",
                                  paste0("US$ ", fmt_n(round(r$total_spend_bn)),
                                         " bn (PPP 2022)"))))
    pairs <- c(pairs, list(list("Studies per million", round(r$per_million, 2))))
    tags$dl(class = "fact-list",
            lapply(pairs, function(p) tagList(tags$dt(p[[1]]), tags$dd(p[[2]]))))
  })
  output$c_n <- renderText(fmt_n(c_row()$studies))
  output$c_daly <- renderText({
    r <- c_row(); m <- c_inc_median()
    if (is.na(r$per100k_dalys)) return("no burden data")
    paste0(round(r$per100k_dalys, 2), "  (median ", round(m$m_daly, 2), ")")
  })
  output$c_spend <- renderText({
    r <- c_row(); m <- c_inc_median()
    if (is.na(r$per_bn_usd)) return("no spending data")
    paste0(round(r$per_bn_usd, 2), "  (median ", round(m$m_bn, 2), ")")
  })
  output$c_percap <- renderText({
    r <- c_row(); m <- c_inc_median()
    paste0(round(r$per_million, 2), "  (median ", round(m$m_mil, 2), ")")
  })

  output$c_trend <- renderPlotly({
    req(input$c_iso3)
    r <- c_row()
    mine <- D$elig_geo |> filter(iso3 == input$c_iso3) |>
      distinct(record_id, year) |> count(year) |> mutate(series = "country")
    n_peer <- n_distinct(D$countries$iso3[D$countries$income == r$income])
    # count each study once per peer country (not once per group), so the mean is
    # comparable with the country series, which counts a study about the country once
    peers <- D$elig_geo |> filter(income == r$income) |>
      distinct(record_id, iso3, year) |> count(year) |>
      mutate(n = n / n_peer, series = "income-group mean")
    s <- bind_rows(mine, peers)
    p <- ggplot(s, aes(year, n, colour = series)) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
      scale_colour_manual(values = c("country" = "#1f5fa8",
                                     "income-group mean" = "#adb5bd"), name = NULL) +
      labs(x = NULL, y = "studies per year") + theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
    ggplotly(p) |>
      layout(legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.18), margin = list(t = 20, b = 60))
  })

  output$c_mix <- renderPlotly({
    req(input$c_iso3)
    r <- c_row()
    ids_mine <- D$elig_geo |> filter(iso3 == input$c_iso3) |> pull(record_id)
    mine <- D$elig_disease |> filter(record_id %in% ids_mine) |>
      count(grp) |> mutate(share = 100 * n / sum(n), series = "country")
    ids_peer <- D$elig_geo |> filter(income == r$income) |> pull(record_id)
    peers <- D$elig_disease |> filter(record_id %in% ids_peer) |>
      count(grp) |> mutate(share = 100 * n / sum(n), series = "income group")
    s <- bind_rows(mine, peers)
    p <- ggplot(s, aes(share, reorder(grp, share), fill = series)) +
      geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.7) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c("country" = "#1f5fa8",
                                   "income group" = "#adb5bd"), name = NULL) +
      labs(x = "share of disease-coded studies (%)", y = NULL) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
    ggplotly(p) |>
      layout(legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.22), margin = list(t = 10, b = 70))
  })
}

name: DEPLOY.md
content:
# HEE evidence-map Shiny app — deploy notes

## Launch

Supported launch (from `projects/hee/analysis`):

```r
shiny::runApp("shiny", launch.browser = TRUE)
```

`runApp` sets the working directory to the app folder, which is where
`app_data.rds`, `intensity.R` and `www/` live. Launching from another cwd also
works (`Rscript shiny/app.R`-style) via the path fallbacks at the top of
`app.R`, but `runApp("shiny")` is the only supported production launch.

## Tested versions (2026-09-09, Windows, R 4.4.1)

| package | version | note |
|---|---|---|
| R | 4.4.1 | ucrt |
| shiny | 1.12.1 | |
| bslib | 0.10.0 | `page_navbar`, `value_box`, `layout_*` APIs |
| dplyr | 1.2.0 | `.data[[ ]]` in `count`/`distinct` needs >= 1.1 |
| ggplot2 | 4.0.0 | |
| **plotly** | **>= 4.12.1** | **4.10.x breaks every `ggplotly()` panel against ggplot2 4.0 ("subscript out of bounds" in `gg2list`)** |
| DT | (any recent) | |
| scales | 1.4.0 | |
| htmltools | (any recent) | |

There is no renv/manifest pinning in this project yet; if the deploy host
resolves packages fresh, enforce `plotly >= 4.12.1` with `ggplot2 4.x`.

Build-side extras (only needed to rebuild the bundle, not to run the app):
readr, countrycode, sf, rnaturalearth, stringr.

## Rebuilding the data bundle

`shiny/app_data.rds`, `shiny/intensity.R` and `shiny/www/*.webp` are build
artifacts produced by:

```
"C:/Program Files/R/R-4.4.1/bin/Rscript.exe" R/09-build-shiny-data.R
```

run from `projects/hee/analysis`. Its inputs (`data/hee_analysis_master.csv`,
`data/hee_geo_long.rds`, `data/mesh_disease_anytopic.csv`, `data/wb_*.csv`,
`projects/hee/data/ihme_health_spending_1995_2022.csv`, the GBD exports and
`figures/*.png`) are **gitignored or untracked** — a fresh clone cannot rebuild
until they are regenerated:

1. `R/00-build-analysis-data.R` (master + geo from the harvested corpus),
2. the fetch scripts for World Bank / GBD / IHME inputs (see `R/fetch-notes-gbd.md`),
3. the `R/fig-*.R` scripts to render `figures/*.png`,
4. then `R/09-build-shiny-data.R`.

The build script warns when any `R/fig-*.R` script is newer than the PNG it
writes (stale-figure guard); re-run the flagged script and rebuild before
shipping.

## Denominator discipline (carried from the audit)

- Income-comparative panels use **extracted geography only**.
- Countries without a World Bank income group (currently Taiwan) are **excluded
  from the country bundle and visibly absent** — never zero-filled as "0 studies".
- Spending totals are IHME THE per capita (PPP, 2022) × **latest** World Bank
  population (mostly 2025); captions must declare both years.
- Open-access filters cover the 93% harvested base; "Unknown" is excluded when
  a side is chosen.

name: intensity.R
content:
# intensity.R -- the single source of truth for research-intensity ratios.
#
# Every "studies per unit of need/money/people" number in the project must be
# computed by these functions: fig-burden-mismatch.R, fig-spending-mismatch.R,
# R/09-build-shiny-data.R and the Shiny app (shiny/app.R sources the copy that
# 09-build-shiny-data.R places in shiny/). The formulas were revised once already
# (audit fix 2026-09-07, eligible base); the next revision must land here once,
# not in four places.
#
# All functions are vectorized and NA-safe: a missing or non-positive denominator
# yields NA_real_ (visibly absent), never Inf and never 0.

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

# Studies per 100,000 DALYs (GBD burden denominator).
per_100k_dalys <- function(studies, dalys) {
  if_else(!is.na(dalys) & dalys > 0, studies / (dalys / 1e5), NA_real_)
}

# Studies per US$1bn of total health expenditure (PPP).
per_bn_usd <- function(studies, spend_bn) {
  if_else(!is.na(spend_bn) & spend_bn > 0, studies / spend_bn, NA_real_)
}

# Studies per million people.
per_million_pop <- function(studies, pop) {
  if_else(!is.na(pop) & pop > 0, studies / (pop / 1e6), NA_real_)
}

# National total health expenditure in PPP US$bn from IHME per-capita THE and
# World Bank population (latest available observation; the year travels with the
# population file and must be declared wherever the total is captioned).
spend_total_bn <- function(the_pc, pop) {
  the_pc * pop / 1e9
}
